newsitem.title: USA: Hong Kong activist Lee backs China MFN.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong activist Lee backs China MFN.

text.p: Hong Kong democracy campaigner Martin Lee on Monday reaffirmed support for continued Most Favored Nation trade status for China and urged U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright to visit the British colony as it reverts to Beijing's control.
Speaking to reporters after talks with Albright, Lee complained that by eroding political and civil freedoms in Hong Kong, China was not helping the campaign for MFN renewal.

Lee also praised President Clinton's decision to meet him later this week, and Albright's decision to see him (on) Monday, as conclusive evidence that the United States "takes the human rights issues very seriously and is prepared to give recognition to the democratic leadership of Hong Kong."

Lee, a Hong Kong legislator and a leading pro-democracy campaigner who heads the colony's Democratic Party, is on a lobbying trip to Washington ahead of July 1, when Hong Kong reverts to China's control under the 1984 Sino-British agreement.

As the transition nears, there is rising concern in the United States that China is not living up to its promises to permit Hong Kong to function as it has, with considerable civil and political freedoms. Increasing numbers of U.S. lawmakers have questioned whether MFN should be renewed.

House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich suggested on Sunday that as a compromise, a renewal of six months, rather than one year, might be in order. Lee said "the Democratic Party and I have always strongly supported the renewal MFN for China unconditionally."
